comparison: Both address the hippocampal inactivation experiment (C12, C77, C84, C86-C89). OpenEval finds the mechanism well-explained and supported by simulations. Peer reviewer expresses difficulty understanding how the model accounts for this experiment, indicating uncertainty about the mechanism rather than rejecting it.

Both evaluate the comparison between STD and SFA mechanisms (C102-C104). OpenEval finds the mechanistic distinction valid and supported. Peer reviewer challenges the claim that Tsodyks & Romani 2015 model cannot produce bidirectional sweeps, demanding proof or removal of the statement, indicating uncertainty about this distinction.

Both address the connection between theta sweeps and replay (C118-C122). OpenEval rates this as uncertain, noting it's speculative and requires further validation. Peer reviewer supports this as a reasonable speculation with no challenges, suggesting acceptance of the hypothesis.

Both evaluate model limitations and idealized assumptions (C123-C124). OpenEval supports the authors' acknowledgment of limitations as appropriate scientific caution. Peer reviewer expresses uncertainty about whether behavior would persist in more realistic models, viewing idealization as the main limitation.

Both address T-maze cycle skipping and alternating sweeps (C10, C67-C71, C73). OpenEval finds this clearly demonstrated and well-explained. Peer reviewer also supports this finding, with the editor highlighting it as a key insight, though noting similarity to prior work.

Both evaluate frequency-speed relationship (C11, C76, C78-C82). OpenEval finds the mechanism well-demonstrated and internally consistent. Peer reviewer finds the result hard to understand and requests better graphical explanation, indicating acceptance of the finding but difficulty with presentation.

Both address predictions about bimodal/unimodal cells and frequency relationships (C90-C92, C113). OpenEval supports these as logical predictions following from model mechanisms. Peer reviewer explicitly endorses these predictions as interesting to experimentalists and requests they be listed prominently.

Both evaluate asymmetric suppression mechanism producing bimodal/unimodal firing patterns (C9, C34-C35, C52, C61-C64). OpenEval finds the mechanism well-explained and supported. Peer reviewer also supports this, with Reviewer 1 calling it especially interesting and Reviewer 2 praising the model's explanatory power.

Both address phase shift mechanism and theta sweeps (C7-C8, C32-C33). OpenEval finds the analytical derivation and simulations clearly demonstrate the mechanism. Peer reviewer strongly supports this as the main result with 'convincing evidence' and 'surprisingly large explanatory power.'

Both evaluate connection between model dynamics and experimental theta sweeps (C5-C6, C30, C46). OpenEval supports the qualitative match to experimental patterns. Peer reviewer also supports this as part of the main result, with all three reviewers endorsing the forward and backward sequences.

Both address theta frequency oscillations (C44-C45). OpenEval supports that oscillation frequency can be tuned to theta range. Peer reviewer expresses uncertainty about robustness, questioning sensitivity to parameter variations and noting lack of evidence for external pacemaker driving theta band oscillations.

Both evaluate model architecture and oscillatory tracking mechanism (C28-C29). OpenEval finds the mathematical formulations and simulations clearly demonstrate the mechanism. Peer reviewer strongly supports this, praising the 'simple yet rather illuminating competition between internally driven and externally driven dynamical trends.'

Both address intrinsic mobility and internally generated dynamics (C27, C38). OpenEval supports the theoretical analysis and validation. Peer reviewer explicitly describes the internally generated traveling-wave dynamics as a key strength of the model.

Both evaluate predictions about asymmetric bump heights (C56-C58). OpenEval supports these as demonstrated predictions. Peer reviewer explicitly endorses this prediction as especially interesting to experimentalists and requests it be listed prominently.

Both address 2D extension (C111). OpenEval supports this as a reasonable extrapolation with preliminary results. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts this straightforward extension through lack of challenge.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about experimental literature and knowledge gaps (C1-C4, C13-C24) as well-supported and providing appropriate motivation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/motivation claims.

OpenEval rates the laminar difference explanation (C65-C66) as uncertain and speculative, requiring experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim about layer-specific adaptation.

OpenEval supports the comparison to existing models (C93-C101) as fair and well-documented, with novel contributions clearly articulated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing the model comparison claims.

OpenEval rates grid cell extension and coordination hypothesis (C115-C117) as uncertain, noting it's presented as future direction without implementation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these grid cell claims.

OpenEval supports claims about functional significance of phase precession (C74-C75) as accurately representing prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these functional context claims.

OpenEval supports the cyclical sweep length prediction (C114) as clearly demonstrated and testable. Peer reviewer R3 mentions this pattern should be 'remarked upon' but doesn't provide separate evaluation; OpenEval treats it as distinct prediction.
